mentions.name: X-Ray Feed
mentions.description: A Chrome MV3 extension that visualizes the Twitter/X ranking algorithm by overlaying the hidden weight of every post directly in the feed. It reverse-engineers the "Heavy Ranker" logic in real time, distinguishing organic content ("Thunder" nodes) from AI-injected recommendations ("Phoenix" nodes), and scores posts with a log10(engagement) × 20 formula to show velocity. All analysis runs locally in the browser, and the tool also serves as an arbitrage aid for identifying "flops" (good topics from big accounts that failed due to structure) that are worth rewriting.
mentions.problem: Guessing why the Twitter/X timeline looks the way it does and telling followed content apart from algorithmic fill; also spotting engagement "flops" from big accounts worth rewriting.
mentions.audience: Guessing why the Twitter/X timeline looks the way it does and telling followed content apart from algorithmic fill; also spotting engagement "flops" from big accounts worth rewriting.
mentions.source_excerpt:
X-Ray Feed – A Chrome extension to visualize the Twitter/X algorithm

I got tired of guessing why my timeline looked the way it did, so I built a tool to reverse-engineer the "Heavy Ranker" logic in real-time.

It’s an MV3 extension that overlays the hidden weight of every post directly in the feed.
